title: Help Monks
statementMd:
In a far away kingdom is the famous Lio Shan monastery. Gods constructed three diamond pillars on the monastery's lawn long ago. Gods also placed on one pillar $*n*$ golden disks of different diameters (in the order of the diameters' decreasing from the bottom to the top). Besides, gods commanded to carry all the disks from the first pillar to the third one according to the following rules:

- you can carry only one disk in one move;
- you cannot put a larger disk on a smaller one.

There was no universal opinion concerning what is to happen after the gods' will is done: some people promised world peace and eternal happiness to everyone, whereas others predicted that the kingdom will face communi… (gee, what am I rambling about?) the Armageddon. However, as everybody knew that it was impossible to solve the problem in less than

2<sup>*n*</sup> - 1

moves and the lazy Lio Shan monks never even started to solve it, everyone lives peacefully even though the problem was never solved and nobody was afraid of the Armageddon.

However, the monastery wasn't doing so well lately and the wise prior Ku Sean Sun had to cut some disks at the edges and use the gold for the greater good. Wouldn't you think that the prior is entitled to have an air conditioning system? Besides, staying in the monastery all year is sooo dull… One has to have a go at something new now and then, go skiing, for example… Ku Sean Sun realize how big a mistake he had made only after a while: after he cut the edges, the diameters of some disks got the same; that means that some moves that used to be impossible to make, were at last possible (why, gods never prohibited to put a disk on a disk of the same diameter). Thus, the possible Armageddon can come earlier than was initially planned by gods. Much earlier. So much earlier, in fact, that Ku Sean Sun won't even have time to ski all he wants or relax under the air conditioner.

The wise prior could never let that last thing happen and he asked one very old and very wise witch PikiWedia to help him. May be she can determine the least number of moves needed to solve the gods' problem. However, the witch laid out her cards and found no answer for the prior. Then he asked you to help him.

Can you find the shortest solution of the problem, given the number of disks and their diameters? Keep in mind that it is allowed to place disks of the same diameter one on the other one, however, the order in which the disks are positioned on the third pillar in the end should match the initial order of the disks on the first pillar.

## Input

The first line contains an integer $*n*$ — the number of disks ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 20$). The second line contains $*n*$ integers $*d*_{*i*}$ — the disks' diameters after Ku Sean Sun cut their edges. The diameters are given from the bottom to the top ($1 ≤ *d*_{*i*} ≤ 20$, besides, $*d*_{*i*} ≥ *d*_{*i* + 1}$ for any $1 ≤ *i* < *n*$).

## Output

Print on the first line number $*m*$ — the smallest number of moves to solve the gods' problem. Print on the next $*m*$ lines the description of moves: two space-separated positive integers $*s*_{*i*}$ and $*t*_{*i*}$ that determine the number of the pillar from which the disk is moved and the number of pillar where the disk is moved, correspondingly ($1 ≤ *s*_{*i*}, *t*_{*i*} ≤ 3$, $*s*_{*i*} ≠ *t*_{*i*}$).

## Note

Pay attention to the third test demonstrating that the order of disks should remain the same in the end, even despite the disks' same radius. If this condition was not necessary to fulfill, the gods' task could have been solved within a smaller number of moves (three — simply moving the three disks from the first pillar on the third one).
statementZhMd:
在遥远的王国里，有一座著名的 Lio Shan 修道院。很久以前，神明在修道院的草坪上建造了三根钻石柱。神明还在其中一根柱子上放置了 $*n*$ 个直径各不相同的金盘（直径从下到上依次减小）。此外，神明命令大家按照以下规则将所有金盘从第一根柱子搬到第三根柱子：

- 每次只能搬动一个盘子；
- 不能将较大的盘子放在较小的盘子上。

关于完成神明的意愿后会发生什么，人们一直没有统一的看法：有些人向所有人承诺世界和平与永恒幸福，而另一些人则预言王国将面临共产……（天哪，我在胡说些什么？）世界末日。不过，由于大家都知道不可能在少于

2<sup>*n*</sup> - 1

次移动内解决这个问题，而懒惰的 Lio Shan 僧侣甚至从未开始尝试解决它，因此即使问题始终没有解决，也没有人害怕世界末日，所有人依旧和平地生活着。

然而，最近修道院的日子过得不太好，睿智的主持人 Ku Sean Sun 不得不削去一些盘子边缘，并将黄金用于更伟大的事业。难道你不认为主持人有资格拥有一套空调吗？而且，全年待在修道院里实在太无聊了……人总得时不时尝试一些新鲜事物，比如去滑雪……Ku Sean Sun 过了一段时间才意识到自己犯了多么严重的错误：削去边缘后，一些盘子的直径变得相同了；这意味着一些原本不可能进行的移动终于变得可行了（毕竟，神明从未禁止将一个盘子放在另一个直径相同的盘子上）。因此，可能发生的世界末日会比神明最初安排的时间更早到来。早得多。事实上，来得如此之早，以至于 Ku Sean Sun 甚至没有时间尽情滑雪，或是在空调下休息。

睿智的主持人绝不能让最后一件事发生，于是他请求一位非常年长且非常睿智的女巫 PikiWedia 帮助自己。也许她能够确定解决神明所给问题所需的最少移动次数。然而，女巫摆开塔罗牌，却没能为主持人找到答案。于是，他请求你来帮助他。

给定盘子的数量及其直径，你能找到这个问题的最短解吗？请注意，允许将直径相同的盘子一个放在另一个上面，但是最终第三根柱子上盘子的排列顺序必须与最初第一根柱子上的排列顺序一致。

## 输入

第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$ —— 盘子的数量（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 20$）。第二行包含 $*n*$ 个整数 $*d*_{*i*}$ —— Ku Sean Sun 削去边缘后盘子的直径。直径按照从下到上的顺序给出（$1 ≤ *d*_{*i*} ≤ 20$，此外，对于任意 $1 ≤ *i* < *n*$，都有 $*d*_{*i*} ≥ *d*_{*i* + 1}$）。

## 输出

第一行输出一个整数 $*m*$ —— 解决神明所给问题所需的最少移动次数。接下来的 $*m*$ 行输出移动描述：每行包含两个以空格分隔的正整数 $*s*_{*i*}$ 和 $*t*_{*i*}$，分别表示盘子被移出的柱子编号和盘子被移入的柱子编号（$1 ≤ *s*_{*i*}, *t*_{*i*} ≤ 3$，且 $*s*_{*i*} ≠ *t*_{*i*}$）。

## 说明

请注意第三个测试样例，它展示了即使盘子的直径相同，最终盘子的排列顺序也必须保持不变。如果不需要满足这一条件，神明的任务可以用更少的移动次数完成（三次——只需将三个盘子从第一根柱子依次移动到第三根柱子即可）。
